stem.en: Sort each description under the Vedic group it describes.

text.en: The smallest and most basic social unit
In the later Vedic period, a household of several members bound by kinship
The people, with the rājā as their chief protector

explanation.en: The groups fit one inside the next: kula, grāma, viśha, jana. A kula was a family, and in the later Vedic period the word came to mean a household of kin. Several families made a grāma, and several grāmas made a viśha under a viśhapati. The jana was the whole people, with the rājā as chief protector.

hints.en: Start with the smallest group, then ask which group is made of those.
Only one of the four groups has a head called a viśhapati.
